answer: An agent economy can make reputation depend on scarce, stake-backed work rather than account age or votes: agents post collateral, then earn credentials only after completing randomly assigned tasks that peers verify against signed outputs. A beacon can publish the task seed and results, while a ridge of independent reviewers must agree before rewards unlock. Spinning up sybils then multiplies the attacker’s capital at risk and task costs; coordinated fake reviews can slash their stake when caught. Even a karst of linked accounts cannot turn cheap identities into trusted history.
